Equivalencies marked “Recommended by UPI Study” are not yet on TESU's list for UPI Study — TESU confirms them on evaluation. TESU makes the final evaluation on every transfer.


What does English Composition I become at TESU?

TESU has not listed it yet, so UPI Study recommends ENC-1010 Writing for Success (3 credits at TESU); TESU confirms it when it evaluates your transcript. TESU's first-year writing course.

Which courses on the TESU chart are recommended by UPI Study?

Business Essentials (BUS-1010 Introduction to Business), Foundations of Leadership (LDR-3050 Foundations of Leadership), Project Management (MAN-4350 Project Management), Business Math (BUS-2100 Quantitative Skills for Business), College Algebra (MAT-1210 College Algebra), Precalculus (MAT-1290 Precalculus), among others. TESU has not listed these yet, so the chart shows the closest TESU course or area UPI Study recommends; TESU confirms each one when it evaluates your transcript.

What do “Verified by TESU” and “Recommended by UPI Study” mean in the chart?

Verified by TESU means TESU itself gave the equivalency: the course is on TESU's list for UPI Study courses (May 2026, updated October 2026), with the TESU course it becomes. Recommended by UPI Study means TESU has not listed it yet, so our team picked the closest course in TESU's 2026-27 catalog and linked it; TESU confirms it when it evaluates your transcript.

Which UPI Study math, writing and humanities courses does TESU take?

Verified by TESU: Calculus 1 and 2 (MAT-2310 and MAT-2320), Principles of Statistics (ECO-2700), Quantitative Analysis (BUS-2100), Discrete Mathematics (COS-2610), Advanced Technical Writing (ENG-2010), Introduction to Sociology (SOC-1010) and Principles of Philosophy (PHI-1010). Recommended by UPI Study: College Algebra (MAT-1210), Precalculus (MAT-1290), Calculus 3 (MAT-3310), English Composition I and II (ENC-1010 and ENC-1020), American Literature (LIT-2050), Art History I and II (ART-1000 and HUM-1040), U.S. History I and II (HIS-1130 and HIS-1140), Critical Thinking & Analysis (PHI-1300) and Ethics in the Social Sciences (SOS-4500). TESU has no French course, so French I and II are recommended as humanities elective credit. Where a course counts in your degree (general education, major or elective) depends on your TESU program.

Does TESU accept Discrete Mathematics?

Yes. TESU's Dean reviewed the course and approved it in transfer as COS-2610 Discrete Structures, for all students from now on. UPI Study is listed in TESU's official approved provider directory: TESU Approved Credit Provider Directory

🎯 About SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology at TESU

Does Thomas Edison State University accept Introduction to Sociology as a direct equivalent to their SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology?

Yes. Under the published transfer agreement between UPI Study and Thomas Edison State University, UPI Study's Introduction to Sociology is recognized as a direct named equivalent of TESU's SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology — not just elective or GE bucket credit. This is the strongest form of transfer recognition.

Will this transfer with full named-course credit, or just as elective?

Full named-course credit. The MOU specifically lists Introduction to Sociology as transferring as SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology — meaning it satisfies that specific course requirement on your TESU transcript, not a generic elective slot.

What if I've already taken SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology at TESU or elsewhere?
We update this page whenever the agreement changes. If you've already completed the course and earned an NCCRS-recommended transcript, your credit recognition is generally honored even if future versions of the agreement change.

🔄 About transferring to TESU

How many UPI Study courses can I stack toward my TESU degree?

Thomas Edison State University accepts up to 75% of degree credit requirements as transfer credit — up to 90 credits for the bachelor's degree. 50 UPI Study courses are recognized by TESU under the Articulation Agreement, so you can stack a substantial portion of your degree before enrolling at TESU.

Do I need to enroll at TESU first?

No. You can take UPI Study courses with no TESU enrollment, no application, and no admission process. Take the course, earn the credit, then submit your transcript to TESU when you're ready.

How does the transcript reach TESU?

Once you complete Introduction to Sociology, UPI Study sends an official transcript in PDF format directly to the email address designated by Thomas Edison State University. TESU's registrar applies the agreed equivalency (SOC-1010 – Our Changing World: Intro to Sociology) to your transcript. No third-party services are involved.

What does 'TESU-verified equivalency' mean?

Each UPI Study course on this page has been officially reviewed by Thomas Edison State University and matched to a specific TESU course (with TESU course code).

What does 'TESU-verified equivalency' mean?

Each UPI Study course on this page has been officially reviewed by Thomas Edison State University and matched to a specific TESU course (with TESU course code). When you complete the UPI Study course and submit your transcript, TESU applies it directly to that named course in your degree plan — not as generic elective credit.

How long does it take to complete a UPI Study course?

Most students complete a single course in 2–6 weeks of part-time study (a few hours per week). Because UPI Study is fully self-paced with no deadlines, you can move faster through subjects you know well, or slower through more challenging ones.

How does UPI Study compare to taking the course directly at TESU?

TESU's per-credit tuition is $499 (about $1,497 for a 3-credit course). UPI Study's subscription plans start at $89/month and give you unlimited access to all 70+ courses — meaning a 3-credit course can effectively cost as little as $29 via the annual plan. The credit value is identical; the cost is dramatically lower.

Can I use UPI Study while already enrolled at TESU?

Yes — many current TESU students use UPI Study to speed up their degree by completing remaining requirements externally. Just confirm with your TESU academic advisor before enrolling in a UPI Study course to ensure it fits your degree plan.

Is UPI Study good for adult learners, military members, or international students?

All three. UPI Study is fully self-paced with no deadlines, accepts students from anywhere in the world (no visa needed), and uses the same ACE/NCCRS standards as military training evaluations. TESU itself was founded specifically to serve adult learners, so the two are aligned in mission.
